settings.personalData.title: Your data
settings.personalData.description: Get a copy of what this instance holds about you, or delete your account permanently.
settings.personalData.deleteConsequences: This is permanent. Your account, your sessions and your team memberships are deleted. Projects you own are not destroyed — they are kept without an owner and stay manageable by an administrator, since they may be shared with a whole team. Your schema edits keep your name in each project's history.

settings.billing.title: License and monetisation

settings.billing.description: You are running the self-hosted open-source build: unlimited projects, SQL exports, real-time collaboration, no license and no subscription. That is currently the only way to run AthanorDB — there is no hosted plan, no billing, and nothing to activate.
settings.billing.apiKeys.intro: Use a key to call the public API (/api/v1) from a script or CI pipeline — read a project's DBML/SQL/SVG, push a schema edit, or trigger a deployment.
settings.billing.apiKeys.createdOnce: Copy this key now — it won't be shown again.
settings.about.title: About and system

teams.visibilityNote: A project with no team assigned is visible to everyone. Assigning a team restricts it to that team's members (plus its creator and administrators).
teams.noneAssigned: No team assigned — visible to everyone.
admin.title: Admin console
admin.deleteUser.title: Delete {{email}}
admin.deleteUser.consequences: Permanently deletes the account, its sessions, its team memberships and the invitations it sent. Changes it made keep its name in each project's history — that record is not rewritten. If you might still need it, disable the account rather than deleting it.
admin.deleteUser.leaveOwnerless: Leave without an owner (only admins will be able to manage them)
admin.resetPassword.title: Reset password — {{email}}
admin.resetPassword.success: Password reset — {{email}} has been signed out everywhere and needs the new password to sign back in.
admin.audit.empty: No actions recorded for this filter.
admin.audit.scopeNote: Only sensitive actions are recorded (deletions, permission changes, exports, account management). Schema edits are not: they already appear in each project's own history, with their author.
admin.errors.empty: No errors recorded for this filter.
admin.errors.scopeNote: Click a row to see its stack trace if one was captured. Unhandled server errors and client-side render crashes (capped at 2000 entries, oldest pruned first) — a debugging aid, not a compliance trail like the audit log.
errorBoundary.title: Something unexpected went wrong
errorBoundary.body: The interface stopped to avoid showing an inconsistent state. Your data is safe: the schema is stored on the server, including the changes made just before the error.
errorBoundary.projectTitle: This project could not be displayed

totp.title: Two-factor authentication

deployment.rollbackConfirmBody: This runs the best-effort inverse of the SQL that was applied. Review it below before continuing.
deployment.rollbackWarningMysql: MySQL cannot run DDL inside a transaction — if this rollback fails partway through, some statements may already be applied. Check the target database afterward.
